---
title: "Physics and mathematics brief for the SandwichedRenyi split"
subtitle: "Why `D̃_α` and `𝐃` should have separate Lean homes"
format: html
---

## The quantities

The Umegaki quantum relative entropy is
$$
D(\rho\|\sigma) = \operatorname{Tr}\bigl[\rho(\log\rho-\log\sigma)\bigr],
$$
with the usual convention that it is infinite when the support of `ρ` is not
contained in the support of `σ`. In PhysLean this is `qRelativeEnt`, with notation
`𝐃(ρ‖σ)`.

The sandwiched Renyi relative entropy is the one-parameter family
$$
\widetilde D_\alpha(\rho\|\sigma)
= \frac{1}{\alpha-1}
  \log \operatorname{Tr}
  \left[
    \left(
      \sigma^{(1-\alpha)/(2\alpha)}
      \rho
      \sigma^{(1-\alpha)/(2\alpha)}
    \right)^\alpha
  \right].
$$

PhysLean writes this family as `D̃_ α(ρ‖σ)` via `SandwichedRelRentropy`.
The Umegaki entropy is represented in the library by the definitional equality

```lean
def qRelativeEnt (ρ σ : MState d) : ENNReal :=
  D̃_1(ρ‖σ)
```

That identity is the mathematical reason for the file split: `𝐃` is the
alpha-equals-one interface, while `D̃_α` is the family that owns the analytic
machinery.

## Why the sandwiched family is its own concept

The sandwiched family is not just a notation around `𝐃`. It carries:

- the spectral trace expression involving
  `σ^((1 - α) / (2 * α)) * ρ * σ^((1 - α) / (2 * α))`;
- the nonnegativity and additivity theory for `D̃_α`;
- the continuity of the map `α ↦ D̃_α(ρ‖σ)`;
- the alpha-equals-one bridge to Umegaki relative entropy;
- the proof machinery using eigenvalues, support projections, and functional
  calculus.

Those are statements about the alpha-family. Keeping them in `Relative.lean`
made `Relative.lean` look like the owner of the family even though the Umegaki
API is only the special case `α = 1`.

## The support convention

The kernel condition in the code,

```lean
σ.M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker
```

is the finite-dimensional expression of
`supp(ρ) ⊆ supp(σ)`. If the condition fails, there is a vector on which `σ` has
zero support but `ρ` does not. Physically, an event can occur under `ρ` but is
impossible under `σ`, so the relative entropy is infinite.

The refactor does not change that convention. It changes where the supporting
proofs live:

- support-sensitive spectral estimates used by the sandwiched family live in
  `SandwichedRenyi.lean`;
- Umegaki-facing support facts such as `qRelativeEnt_ker` and
  `qRelativeEnt_eq_top_iff` stay in `Relative.lean`.

## Lower semicontinuity

Lower semicontinuity of `𝐃(ρ‖σ)` is a key analytic property: it says relative
entropy cannot jump downward under limiting perturbations of `σ`. This matters
for approximation arguments, compactness arguments, and optimization over state
spaces.

The first split left `qRelativeEnt.lowerSemicontinuous` in `Relative.lean` with a
proof depending on eigen-weight internals from the sandwiched engine. That was a
bad ownership boundary: it forced implementation details of the sandwiched
spectral proof to be public.

The final refactor instead proves the family-facing theorem

```lean
sandwichedRelRentropy_one_lowerSemicontinuous :
  LowerSemicontinuous fun σ => D̃_1(ρ‖σ)
```

inside `SandwichedRenyi.lean`. The Umegaki theorem then follows by the definition
of `qRelativeEnt`.

This is both better Lean organization and better mathematics: the alpha-family
owns the alpha-equals-one analytic bridge, while `Relative.lean` owns only the
Umegaki name and wrapper API.

## What this PR does not claim

This PR does not introduce a new proof of a physical theorem. The earlier
joint-convexity submission closed a mathematical gap. This PR is a structural
refactor that makes the existing quantum-information API easier to review,
maintain, and extend.

The physics contribution is therefore architectural: it aligns the formal file
structure with the conceptual structure used by quantum information theory.
Sandwiched Renyi relative entropy is a family; Umegaki relative entropy is the
alpha-equals-one endpoint. The Lean modules should reflect that.
